messages:
maya: Quick synthesis from this month's incident harvest — we have 6 near-duplicates where late KV cache eviction + cold-starting model workers spiked tail latency. Putting together a short playbook and owner handoff.

ian: thanks. can you paste the list? I can take ownership of warmup scripts.

maya: sure — linked the incident IDs: INC-1821, INC-1837, INC-1850, INC-1863, INC-1899, INC-1904. top recurring causes:
- kv cache TTL misconfig (4x)
- pod warmup not firing on scale (3x)
- overloaded shared batchers (2x)

sophia: noted. i'll add batcher throttles to the backlog. estimated PR for throttles: 2w.

lee: @ian if you own warmup, can you add a short checklist? we need rollout + canary and a fallback to smaller batcher.

ian: def. initial plan:
1) add proactive warmup join on pod create
2) add healthcheck that verifies kv cache priming
3) rollout 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 8h with rollback on latency regressions
I'll open PR tomorrow. cc @maya

maya: thanks. couple of action items for tracking sheet:
- OWNER: ian, TASK: warmup scripts + canary, DUE: 2026-04-14
- OWNER: sophia, TASK: batcher throttles + gating, DUE: 2026-04-21
- OWNER: lee, TASK: infra alerts + dashboards for kv TTL anomalies, DUE: 2026-04-09

sophia: added to my board. can we also add a regression test tied to the postmortem prompt set?

maya: yes please. add TEST: end-to-end latency regression using pm-set 'kv-evict-regen'.

incident-bot: Linked postmortems: https://redwood.internal/postmortem/INC-1821, INC-1837

lee: quick note — for dashboards I'll create a composite metric 'service.kv_eviction_rate' and alert at 0.5% spike.

ian: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infer/warmup#1234 — contains warmup hook + healthcheck. requesting review from @sophia @lee

sophia: reviewing now. small comment on timing for retries.

maya: let's sync next Wed 10am to confirm rollout and close action items. if anyone can't make it, add updates in the thread.

lee: ok for me. :thumbsup:

ian: works for me.

sophia: yep

maya: thanks all — goal: reduce recurrence by 80% in next month; tracking in the incident patterns doc.
